detail.longDescription:
Possibly it would make more sense to ask on the 196 community based on the
company’s energy. Anyway, I was browsing EURid’s list of registrars
[https://eurid.eu/en/get-your-eu/find-a-registrar/], and this company’s logo
took my attention. However, I can’t find any experiences online. I’ve checked
through their websites, and so far my feelings are a bit mixed. Although most of
it is just outdated or somewhat inconsistent bits across their websites. #
Things that make me unsure First and least important is info about one of the
people behind the company, “Alfie”. Links on the about page
[https://glauca.digital/about/] are just completely outdated and dead. Website
link in docs [https://docs.glauca.digital/oid/] is at least alive, but also
outdated, as can be seen by navigating in manner of URL in docs -> keybase ->
GitHub -> newer website.
Second, the “Email us” button on the contact page
[https://glauca.digital/contact/] redirects to a contact form, which really
contradicts the text below:
> If you want to send us a PGP encrypted email, please use the below key.
Remember to attach your own key (as application/pgp-keys), so we can encrypt our
reply to you.
That sounded so cool when I’ve seen it, but what e-mail address?
The contact form is on a “support” subdomain of their other website. This seems
to be centered around the contact form, but there is also a “Manage PGP keys”
button which redirects to a login page.
Maybe they migrated to that?
But then going to contact page on the domain’s second level
[https://as207960.net/contact.html] does show an email, as well as linking to
the same contact form. Third, in the list of services, there’s also “Email
[https://mail.glauca.digital/]”… which presents a self-signed certificate.
Ignoring that, there’s just an “Unknown URL” error page.
> We’re probably not responsible for this domain. Lastly, and most importantly,
right on ther main page it says: > Proxy registration for .eu And that’s the
only mention of that feature. But what is it? If following ICANN’s definition
[https://www.icann.org/resources/pages/privacy-proxy-registration-2013-03-22-en]…
> Proxy Services – Proxy services allow a domain name to keep certain identity
and contact details from appearing in public Whois information. The proxy
service becomes the registered name holder of record, and its identity and
contact information is displayed in Whois data. …it might be a problem. Because,
let’s take a look at T&C of EURid (PDF)
[https://cdn.eurid.eu/assets/terms_and_conditions-2.pdf]: > Throughout the Term
of your Domain Name registration, you must: > […] > b. keep your registration
data accurate, complete and up-to-date at all times. Your registration data must
be your own data and must not be that of your Registrar, or of a proxy holder or
a representative of a natural person or legal entity who does not meet the
eligibility criteria. […] There’s also an annoying requirement for tax reasons,
but that’s not their fault: > In short things are about to get a lot more
complicated. We will need to collect at least two pieces of non contradictory
evidence about which country you’re resident in, so we can pay the correct tax
authority. # And what caught my attention (in a good way) As I’ve said, I
checked them based on their logo. That’s not a usual company logo. Pricing for
.eu TLD is OK. Their ToS is short. One button on bottom says “there’s no ai
here!”. Looking at the about page [https://glauca.digital/about/], this seems to
be a small company operated by 2 people. Looking at their mailing list archive
[https://listmonk.as207960.net/archive], they’ve used to have a VPS service,
gave shutdown information in advance (though less than 2 months), and set-up a
migration route with another provider.
They’ve also informed about a security incident at one of their registries.
WHOIS privacy includes email forwarding from a funny domain name:
> If you do not select it we will generate an anonymous @owowhosth.is email and
publish that instead. On their Mastodon, they describe themselves with > On a
mission to make interneting a little easier, join us at http://glauca.digital/
[http://glauca.digital/]. Possibly anarchist, definitely antifascist. Oh, and
speaking of Mastodon, that is listed as one of their services. Based on this
disclaimer… > MOBILE APP USERS: if you’re trying to sign up with a mobile app go
back and select login to authenticate with our SSO. …it does indeed sound like
being their customer includes account on their Mastodon instance. Pretty cool if
true. Also, try whois with their ASN:
<> aut-num: AS207960 as-name: AS-TRANSRIGHTS descr: Trans Rights! Hell Yeah!
